step_by_step_reasoning: First, we identify the main actors: public users requesting HTML content, and developer/newsroom users managing templates and code. Public requests hit an ECS-based origin proxy, which either fetches static/pre-rendered content from S3 buckets, or triggers dynamic rendering via AWS Lambda on cache misses. Newsroom users define web templates stored in DynamoDB, which Lambda reads during execution. During rendering, Lambda fetches content through a secondary ECS-based CMS proxy that queries external CMS platforms and stores raw content in ElastiCache to speed up subsequent requests.
